activities.caption: file the preparation moves — what does each buy?
activities.name: ivPrepBuckets

config.prompt: Reading everything first does three jobs at once. File each payoff:

items.label: the live interview kept for what only the subject can supply
the evidence folder, printed and tabbed

config.why: Accountability interviews run on paper — and the question list is a map, not a script.

activities.caption: pair each question family with what it buys
activities.name: ivQuestionMatch

config.prompt: Questions come in families, and each buys something different:

pairs.right: pinning facts and locking a position on the record
worthless confirmation — the honest form is presenting the evidence
the subject answers whichever half is easier

config.why: A well-formed question is short, single and concrete — then the craft moves to what happens after it.

activities.anchor: a story with numbers in it
activities.caption: bet first — the most under-used tool
activities.name: ivSilencePredict

config.q: The subject says the launch 'was chaos'. The professional says nothing for two seconds. What arrives in the gap?
choices: Unprepared material — often the sentence they had decided not to say
config.why: People fill conversational gaps, and what they volunteer is the second answer: 'We had two servers and one engineer, and on launch morning the database crashed for four hours.' The first answer was a claim; the second is a story with numbers in it.

activities.anchor: the response is frequently newsworthy in itself
activities.caption: file the interview types — which instrument, which rules?
activities.name: ivAccountBuckets

config.prompt: Interviews divide by intent. File each feature:

items.label: runs on rapport: genuine curiosity, the subject talking more than you
hard questions come after the basics, so there is a record to test

config.why: The request is always for response — the fairness duty AND a reporting technique, because the denial that contradicts the document is newsworthy in itself.

activities.anchor: agree the description's wording with the source
activities.caption: rebuild the attribution ladder
activities.name: ivLadderOrder

config.prompt: From most to least usable — order the ladder:
items: On the record: everything usable, attributed by name and title
On background: usable, source described by role — wording agreed with the source
Deep background: guides the reporting, cannot be quoted or attributed
Off the record: for the reporter's understanding, not publishable
config.why: The discipline is to negotiate the level before the answer, never after — a source who says 'off the record' after speaking has, strictly, no claim to it.

activities.anchor: the subject's trust more than by the interviewer's control
activities.caption: true or false — trauma-aware practice
activities.name: ivTraumaJudge

statements.s: Trauma-aware interviewing is about comfort, at the cost of rigour.
statements.why: The evidence runs the other way: pressure produces cautious, rehearsed or contaminated accounts, while a witness who controls the pace gives fuller, more accurate detail.

statements.s: Informed consent means explaining what publication means and reach, before the person has invested in telling you.
statements.why: Consent first — investment later makes the withdrawal cost cruel.

statements.s: Press for the worst moment early, so the rest of the interview feels easier.
statements.why: Approach through neutral ground — 'tell me about the morning' — and let the subject set the boundary.

statements.s: What was said in a fragile moment may deserve more care than what was technically quotable.
statements.why: Dignity in the edit is one of the codified duties.

activities.anchor: never read quotes back for approval
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the quote contract
activities.name: ivQuoteSpot

config.prompt: One line of this quote-handling routine is wrong — click it:
lines: Record with consent, and take notes anyway — recorders fail.
Tidy stumbles that do not change meaning: 'gonna' becomes 'going to'.
Rearrange and trim the quote so the sense better fits the story's angle.
Never read quotes back for approval — once on the record, the quote is published as said.
config.correction: You may tidy stumbles that do not change meaning; you may not rearrange, trim to flip sense, or clean up grammar into something the person did not say.
config.why: The tape protects both sides: every disputed quote resolves to the recording — 'I was misquoted' is the most common complaint in journalism.
